diagnosis: Either: Compares numbers by focusing on individual large digits instead of the highest place value. Or: Believes the number with the larger sum of digits is greater.
rationale: The student thought 3,999 was greater than 4,001 because of the digit 9. Using a place-value comparison demonstration will explicitly show comparing starting from the greatest place value (thousands) where 4 thousands beats 2 thousands regardless of trailing digits.

script.focus: Compare the thousands place first: 3 thousands is more than 2 thousands.

intent: Demonstrate compare on the place-value with values [2999,3001]. Tutor points at: Compare the thousands place first: 3 thousands is more than 2 thousands.

frames.caption: Line up 2,999 and 3,001 by place. Start with the biggest place.
3 thousands is more than 2 thousands, so 3,001 is greater than 2,999. The smaller places cannot catch up, even if they are 9s.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly addresses the exact misconception ('even if they are 9s, the smaller places cannot catch up') using an analogous pair of numbers (2,999 vs 3,001 instead of 3,999 vs 4,001). A worked demo lowers the cognitive demand to purely observing the rule.
judgement.verdict: Yes, a teacher would definitely use this clear, worked demonstration to explicitly counter the belief that having 9s in smaller places makes a number larger.
